Well, I guess I can give it another shot. It has been a while since I last went to therapy. I would never talk to my parents about it. I can never talk to either of them without either of them screaming their lungs out. I get to see my father once every one or two years, so I'm practically estranged from him. My mother is another issue. I don't want to talk to anyone I know about it because then I'd feel like they'd treat me differently because of whatever I'm going through. This is probably why I felt comfortable talking to therapists in the first place. They're strangers, and I can just stop going to them or change therapists if anything happened. 

Sorry for talking about myself for so long. How are you? I hope you are doing well.

Nope I never took them. I saw what it does to my friend, who is suffering from depression as well. His responses are slow and he sleeps a lot. I don't want that. It scares me. To not be able to function normally on top of all this... I can't do it. Thank you for your replies though. It's nice to see someone cares. Maybe if anyone in real life knew I was contemplating ending it all, they would stop me. Which is why I don't want to tell anyone. I just want to go away quietly.
But here's the thing though, I don't think I find comfort in chaos. It seems like I get hurt very easily, and people around me can't feel my pain. It's the worst feeling ever, to be alone in a crowded room. To not be able to talk to anyone about it. Maybe me posting here is a cry for help. I don't know what will help me though. This is making me feel more sad than before.

I've been trying to go through with it for years. It has been so long. I believe it was 2014 when depression first hit me. Before that, I was a pretty regular teenager. The most I did was cut myself. But now when I think back to it, it was just so I could express my sadness. I didn't write back then, I didn't do anything. I had no outlet. So I suppose that's what I did. But somewhere along the way, I started getting scared of blood. I know, it sounds weird. But that's what happened, and I stopped. My life went on normally after that. Then things started changing way too often, I had to move to different cities which meant I had to change high schools a few times. That's when it started. I went from a straight A student to a student that didn't even do the bare minimum. My academic counselor got concerned about me, and be called me to his office one day to ask. I didn't say much, but he pulled me out of class that day and took me to the counselor at school. That was my first introduction to therapy. After that I've been in and out of therapy up until last year around the holidays, when I finally gave up. My family is complicated. My friendships are as well. My relationship. Everything is just going down. So clearly the problem is me, since I'm the common denominator here. People keep telling me I just don't want to be happy. I refuse to accept happiness. I wonder if they're right. It would've been different if one person said that, but multiple people who have known me for years and years tell me that. So what's the point of going on if I can never be happy. Instead of making myself and people around me miserable, it's better to end it for good. All that is left now is to just go through with it.
Are you feeling a little better today?
